props.label: About Us
props.heading: No surprises at the destination
props.body:
We have been putting trips together since 2009, and almost everything we sell is something one of us has travelled first.

Our quotes list what is included and — more usefully — what is not. Entry fees, tips, and the meals you are actually going to buy for yourself are all written down before you pay anything.

One coordinator stays with your booking from the first enquiry through to the day you land back. You will not be handed between desks halfway through.

props.label: Holiday Packages
props.heading: Trips you can book today
props.sub: Prices are per person and change with duration and room sharing — pick your options on any package to see the exact fare. Flights are quoted separately unless stated.

items.title: Golden Triangle — Delhi, Agra & Jaipur
items.desc: The classic first trip through North India: Old Delhi, the Taj at sunrise, and the forts and bazaars of Jaipur.
items.body:
The route most people do first, and for good reason.

You start in Delhi with Humayun's Tomb and a walk through Chandni Chowk, drive to Agra for the Taj at sunrise — which is genuinely worth the early start — then on to Jaipur for Amber Fort, the City Palace and Hawa Mahal.

Included: air-conditioned car with driver throughout, hotels with breakfast, and a licensed local guide at each city. Not included: monument entry fees (roughly ₹2,600 per person for the full circuit), lunches and dinners, and anything you buy in the bazaars.

Best between October and March. April to June is workable but genuinely hot.

items.title: Kerala Backwaters & Hills
items.desc: A night on a private houseboat through the Alleppey backwaters, then tea country and cool air in Munnar.
items.body:
Slow, green and about as restful as India gets.

You spend a full night on a private houseboat drifting through the Alleppey backwaters — meals cooked on board, no schedule to keep — then head up to Munnar for tea estates, a plantation walk and genuinely cold mornings.

Included: houseboat with all meals, hotels with breakfast, and a private car with driver throughout. Not included: flights, lunches and dinners on the land portion, and entry to the tea museum.

September to March is ideal. The monsoon months are beautiful and much cheaper, but expect rain most days.

items.title: Rajasthan Heritage Circuit
items.desc: Jaipur, Jodhpur and Udaipur — forts, stepwells and a lake palace, at a pace that isn't punishing.
items.body:
Three cities, each with a completely different character.

Jaipur for Amber Fort and the bazaars, Jodhpur for Mehrangarh standing over the blue city, and Udaipur for the lake and a slower couple of days at the end.

We keep the driving to a maximum of five hours in any one day, which is the difference between enjoying Rajasthan and enduring it.

Included: private AC car with driver, heritage-property hotels with breakfast, and licensed guides in each city. Not included: monument entry fees, meals other than breakfast, and the Udaipur boat ride.

productInfo.label: Max drive
productInfo.value: About 5 hours on any single day

items.title: Goa — Beaches & Old Town
items.desc: North Goa's beaches and shacks, plus a half-day through the churches and lanes of Old Goa.
items.body:
An easy long weekend, or a slower week if you take the six-night option.

You stay in North Goa within reach of the beaches and shacks, with a half-day through Old Goa's churches and a lazy river cruise if the weather plays along.

Included: hotel with breakfast, airport transfers and the Old Goa half-day tour. Not included: flights, most meals, and water sports.

November to February is peak and prices rise accordingly. The shoulder months are quieter and noticeably cheaper.

items.title: Island Escape — Beaches & Snorkelling
items.desc: White sand, clear water and reef snorkelling, with ferry transfers and beach-front stays arranged.
items.body:
For anyone whose idea of a holiday is water, and not much else.

Beach-front stays, reef snorkelling with a guide, and inter-island ferry transfers handled for you — the part most people get wrong when they book independently.

Included: stays with breakfast, ferry transfers, and one guided snorkelling session. Not included: flights to the gateway airport, diving certification, and meals beyond breakfast.

Tell us at enquiry whether you want the quieter islands or the livelier ones; it changes the itinerary quite a bit.

items.title: Greek Islands — Santorini & Athens
items.desc: Athens for the Acropolis, then the caldera villages of Santorini. Visa assistance included.
items.body:
Two nights in Athens for the Acropolis and the old town, then the ferry across to Santorini for the caldera villages, sunsets at Oia and a day on the black-sand beaches.

Included: hotels with breakfast, inter-island ferry, airport transfers and full Schengen visa assistance. Not included: international flights, travel insurance, and meals beyond breakfast.

Apply for the visa at least eight weeks ahead — appointment slots are the usual bottleneck, not the paperwork.

items.q: Are flights included in the package price?
items.a: No — package prices cover land arrangements only, so you can use your own miles or preferred airline. We are happy to quote flights separately and book them alongside the trip.

items.q: What does the price actually cover?
items.a: Accommodation with breakfast, transport as described, and any guides or activities listed on the package page. Every package also states what is NOT included, which is usually monument fees, most meals, tips and personal spending.

items.q: How much do I pay upfront?
items.a: Twenty-five per cent confirms the booking. The balance is due fifteen days before departure. For international trips with visa processing we ask for the balance earlier — the exact schedule is on your invoice.

Cancel more than thirty days out and you lose only the deposit. Between thirty and fifteen days it is fifty per cent, and inside fifteen days no refund is possible as hotels and transport are already paid. Date changes are free once, more than thirty days out.
Yes, on international packages we handle documentation and the appointment. We cannot influence the decision, and visa fees are paid directly by you to the consulate.

items.q: Can you build a custom itinerary?
items.a: That is most of what we do. Tell us roughly where, when, how long and a budget range, and we will send a draft itinerary with costs within two working days.
It is not included, but we strongly recommend it and can arrange a policy at the time of booking. For most international destinations it is effectively mandatory for the visa.

props.heading: Somewhere else in mind?
props.sub: Most of our trips start as a custom itinerary. Tell us where, when and roughly your budget, and we'll send a draft plan with costs in two working days.

props.label: Get In Touch
props.heading: Tell us about your trip
props.sub: Where you want to go, rough dates, how many of you and a budget range — that's enough for us to send a first itinerary.

notes: Built on the `products` section: packages carry Duration x Occupancy (or Hotel grade) attributes with a per-combination fare, which is how holidays are genuinely priced — per person, on sharing. Some combinations are stock 0 so the sold-out state shows in a demo. Every destination photo was identified before its package was named, so titles match what is actually pictured (Taj, Hawa Mahal, India Gate, Kerala backwaters, Goa, Santorini); the one generic tropical-beach shot is deliberately titled 'Island Escape' rather than claiming a specific island. Cancellation, payment and visa answers in the FAQ are plausible industry defaults, NOT legal advice — an operator must replace them with their own terms before going live. Photos are hosted Unsplash URLs (SiteRenderer::media passes any http(s) URL through) — replace them with the operator's own before going live.
